# Post Hoc Power {#post-hoc-power}

<div class="draft">Work in progress.</div>

Question: why not work out power afterwards?

Observed power = power calculated from the effect you found. It is the p-value in disguise.

Setup

- mindfulness experiment, true d = 0.4, 50 per group, true power about .51
- 5000 labs, each works out its own observed power

Reality 1: one number in two costumes

- plot observed power against p: every dot on one curve
- p = .05 gives observed power about .50
- so every non-significant result has observed power under .50; "we were underpowered" is guaranteed, not evidence

Reality 2: it misses the true power

- every lab's true power is .51
- observed power spreads from near 0 to near 1 (middle 80%: about .11 to .91)
- histogram with the true value as a line

Reality 3: the backwards argument

- two non-significant labs, p = .06 and p = .60
- p = .06 has higher observed power, which would read as the "more convincing null"

Instead

- redo one lab's write-up with a sensitivity analysis (previous chapter) and a CI

Toolbox: `my_observed_power(p, n)`.
